stem.en: A Daniell cell at 1.1 volts and a torch cell at 1.5 volts each run an LED until dead. Kabir says "the torch cell must deliver more energy, because 1.5 is more than 1.1". What else matters?

text.en: How much charge each can pass before its reactants are used up. A big Daniell cell with a lot of zinc can deliver far more total energy than a tiny torch cell, despite the lower volts.

feedback.en: Volts are per electron. Total energy needs the number of electrons, which depends on how much zinc and copper sulphate there is.
The LED decides how fast the energy is used, not how much there is.
A blue LED needs about 3 volts to light at all, which is a different point: neither cell alone will light it. Total energy is still volts times charge.

explanation.en: Volts times charge. Volts are fixed by the reaction. Charge is fixed by how much reactant there is to fall.
